misconceptions.description: Believing instructor-side setup facts (links work, modules visible) prove the course is ready
misconceptions.trigger: checklist verifies setup but never tests whether a student can complete the capstone
misconceptions.feedback: Check readiness against the student's path, not the setup; a working link is not a usable scaffold.

misconceptions.description: Assigning a capstone panel (evidence, limitations, transfer) with no earlier activity that practiced it
misconceptions.trigger: a required capstone sub-skill has no prior building activity in the course
misconceptions.feedback: Trace each capstone panel back to a building activity; front-loading new demands at the capstone overloads learners.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a policy in the syllabus is effective even when it is never referenced where it applies
misconceptions.trigger: an assignment that requires disclosure does not link to the AI-use clause it depends on
misconceptions.feedback: Reference the policy at the point of use so students connect the requirement to the rule.
